RECOMMENDATION: IT DEPENDS
LIKELIHOOD: 35

An all-male panel is not evidence of discrimination by itself — economics faculties are heavily male, so this happens by chance often. Treated as your main argument, it looks weak and personalises the dispute.

Your strong facts are objective: completed PhD vs. unfinished, six papers vs. two, four years of teaching for a teaching post. And a public body ignoring a written request for reasons for two weeks is itself a problem, often a legal duty.

So: pursue it, but lead with the credentials gap and the missing explanation. Send a formal follow-up citing the relevant access-to-reasons rule. Mention panel composition only as context if the stated reasons turn out not to withstand scrutiny.
